evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Etymology Database, CUHK)
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 一 entry
evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone and bronze forms represent the concept of one with an abstract horizontal stroke, and that these forms and the small-seal form use one horizontal stroke for the number one. It cites oracle-bone 《合集》21575「一牛」 as a numeral use. The page also discusses 弌 as a more complex form: it reports the received Shuowen label 古文一, then gives a later proposal deriving the shape through 戈 and 一, and marks the suggested 戌-based precursor as unattested and tentative. This is a source account, not independent verification of every proposed graphic transition.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析 — 一

evidence.source: 說文解字在線查詢 Shuowen.org
evidence.field: 一 entry; received definition and 弌 label
evidence.text: The page gives the received Shuowen explanation 惟初太始，道立於一，造分天地，化成萬物 and says characters in the 一 category follow 一. It labels 弌 古文一. This is the Han dictionary's cosmological explanation and classification, not direct evidence that the graph originally depicted heaven or earth. The page also reproduces Duan Yucai's Qing-period commentary calling the graph an indicative form; that is a later interpretation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「一」

evidence.text: Official record for U+4E00 gives current kMandarin yī and kDefinition “one; a, an; alone.” This is present-day character metadata; it does not date those senses or establish their semantic order. The local Unihan_Readings.txt row checked for 一 is kMandarin yī, in agreement with this official page.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E00

evidence.text: The inspected table gives Mandarin yī, Middle Chinese 'jit and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ʔi[t], glossed ‘one’ (GSR 0394a). The exact local row in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv was checked and matches those MC and OC forms. These are readings of 一 as a word/character, not evidence for its graphic origin or a sound-component role.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.text: The same table gives 壹 Mandarin yī, Middle Chinese 'jit and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ʔi[t], gloss ‘one’ (GSR 0395a). The checked local row agrees. This reading comparison does not establish the chronology or direction of use between 壹 and 一.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

gaps: The CUHK character page's direct fetch timed out; its search result exposed the entry text and citation 《合集》21575「一牛」. No date or archaeological context for that specific inscription was recovered, so it is reported as an oracle-bone attestation without a more exact date.
No dated lexical history was recovered for the senses ‘a/an’ or ‘alone’; they are listed by modern Unihan metadata and are not ordered here as historical extensions.

The source material supports the graph as a numeral written with a horizontal stroke, but this pass did not independently establish an exact chronological sequence of graphic variants across all periods or evidence for graphic corruption. The tentative 戌-based proposal for 弌 is explicitly unverified in the CUHK account.
The received Shuowen cosmological account is not proof that 一 originally depicted heaven or earth. No separate semantic-development claim is made.
No phonetic or semantic subcomponent analysis or phonetic-loan proposal is warranted for this basic graph account.

Local rows checked: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt for 一 and sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv for 一 and 壹. These local checks support provenance only; the cited external Unicode and Baxter–Sagart pages provide click-through evidence. The official Unihan query for U+58F9 was attempted but inaccessible; the table provides the 壹 comparison.

No bulk dataset extract is recommended; the character-specific findings are sufficient and reuse terms for recurring textual material were not established. Image rights were checked only for the specific selected Commons redrawings.

limitations.text: The Commons image files were not visually inspected in this research stage. Their file descriptions establish identity, script labels, provenance claims and stated reuse rights; a later pixel inspection should confirm the rendered forms.
The oracle redraw is attributed to Sinica and other character databases, but the underlying artifact and its inscription date are not specified by the image description.
